hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: `python tools/gdl/fnasm.py game/sys/memcard drawMemCardMessage 0xc0:0xd4 --raw --diff` plus the same view at 0x1e8:0x200, which is where the quoted words above come from: if every path from `@0xc4 b ->0xd0` to `@0x1ec addi r3,r25,0` passes through `@0xcc mr r25,r3`, the entry component is unreachable and the flag is the screen's, not the function's. `--depth 6` on the screen changes nothing here, because the disagreement is at a phi element and not at the depth limit.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes -- every instruction quoted above was read from the aligned raw view against the retail object, and the offset is independently recorded by the CE census as the value-equality relation's refusal point. NOT checked: whether the `@0xc4` branch's path can reach +0x1ec, which is the observation above.
hypothesis.statement: The operand-provenance screen's one open FINDING is game/sys/memcard::drawMemCardMessage at +0x1ec, the same word claim.CE_constant-equality-closure-demand-census-image-wide.20260903.v1 records the shipped value-equality relation refusing at. Both streams have exactly ONE in-function definition of the compared register and it is the same call result -- target `@0xcc mr r25,r3` against ours `@0xcc mr r28,r3`, both taking `@0xc8 bl MBNewTempQuad`'s return -- and the compared use is target `@0x1ec addi r3,r25,0` against ours `@0x1ec addi r3,r28,0`. What makes the screen report a value difference rather than a renaming is the branch `@0xc4 b ->0xd0`, which skips that definition: on that path the register carries its INCOMING value, so the reaching-definition set is a two-element phi and its second element is the entry value of a DIFFERENT architectural register on each side. The next lane should decide whether that path can reach +0x1ec at all. If it cannot, the phis collapse to the shared call result and this row is a false positive of the screen's weakest evidence class; if it can, the two streams read a genuinely different value there and the function is not a recolor.
